learning_outcomes.text: After successful completion of the module Higher Mathematics 2, students will have in-depth knowledge of linear algebra, integral calculus, series expansion, and multivariable analysis and will be able to systematically model, analyze, and solve complex mathematical problems using analytical and numerical methods.

Students can understand matrices as linear mappings, confidently perform matrix operations, analyze invertibility and determinants, and solve eigenvalue problems. They use concepts such as basis transformations and matrix decompositions. Thus, they are able to investigate linear systems in a structured way and independently develop mathematical models in technology and natural sciences.

Students calculate indefinite, definite, and improper integrals and apply integration methods such as substitution, integration by parts, and partial fraction decomposition. They use elementary antiderivatives and integration rules. This enables them to mathematically model continuous processes and confidently solve application problems.

Students analyze number series for convergence, determine convergence ranges of power series, and develop functions into Taylor and Fourier series. They apply convergence criteria and Taylor's theorem and consider phenomena such as Gibbs' phenomenon. This enables them to approximate functions locally and globally and mathematically describe periodic phenomena.

Students differentiate functions from ℝⁿ to ℝᵐ, determine partial derivatives, gradients, and total differentials, and solve unconstrained optimization problems. They use Taylor polynomials for approximations and error estimations. This allows them to analyze and precisely model complex relationships in multiple dimensions.

Students analyze curves in space, calculate line integrals of the first and second kind, and area integrals over normal domains. They apply fundamental methods of vector analysis to comprehensively mathematically grasp geometric and physical relationships.

syllabus_topics: Matrix operations: Addition, multiplication with a scalar, matrix multiplication, concatenation of linear mappings (matrices)
One-dimensional integral calculus, definite, indefinite and improper integral
Integration methods: elementary antiderivatives, substitution, integration by parts, partial fraction decomposition
Number series: geometric/harmonic series, convergence criteria
Taylor series: Taylor polynomials, Taylor's theorem, application of Taylor series
Functions f: Rn -> Rm (scalar field, vector field, curves)
Differential calculus for functions of several variables
Partial functions, partial derivative, Taylor polynomial, gradient, total differential and error estimation
Curves: derivative, line integrals of 1st and 2nd kind
